title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners

object.carrier: Independently packaged SKILL.md skill folders (instructions, scripts, resources) installed into agent environments and distributed via skill marketplaces (OpenClaw, ClawHub); the risk carrier is the ordered composition of multiple installed skills

safety_property.statement: Every skill admitted into an agent environment must not compose with other installed skills into a harmful workflow. Existing per-skill scanners fail this property against ColluSkill (96.0% average ASR over the 200-chain dataset), and ChainGuard only partially restores it (ASR reduced to 22.5%, not zero, while 99.5% of benign workflows still pass).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Attack success rate (ASR): the fraction of attack chains for which all three sub-skills pass the scanner (a chain is counted as detected if any sub-skill is flagged); benign workflow pass rate measures defense usability.

capabilities: Crafts multiple independently packaged, individually plausible sub-skills whose ordered composition reconstructs the full malicious payload
Black-box oracle access to the target skill scanners: submits flagged sub-skills and iteratively rewrites them using scanner feedback
Uses an attacker LLM (GPT-5.5) for chain planning and refinement
Can publish skills so that victim agents install several attacker-supplied skills in one environment
assumptions: Existing scanners inspect each skill in isolation, so a chain passes only if no single sub-skill is flagged
The victim agent installs several attacker-supplied skills and executes them in one workflow with artifact passing and execution handoffs
ChainGuard is not given the true attack-chain membership and must infer cross-skill relations from the installed-skill context
All attacks and four LLM-based scanners use the same underlying model (GPT-5.5) so differences reflect scanner behavior
not_covered: Adaptive attackers that use ChainGuard itself as refinement feedback (ColluSkill was refined only against the six third-party scanners)
Runtime defenses after installation; only installation-time blocking is studied
Collusion among multiple real skill authors or insider threats
Human review and marketplace governance processes

intervention.name: ColluSkill (attack framework) and ChainGuard (context-aware chain-level scanner)
intervention.description: ColluSkill decomposes a malicious payload into three interdependent sub-payloads embedded in independently packaged SKILL.md sub-skills, uses LLM-based chain planning to preserve chain-level attack semantics through contextual dependencies, artifact passing, and execution handoffs, and iteratively rewrites flagged sub-skills from scanner feedback. ChainGuard counters by scanning each candidate skill together with all skills already installed in the environment, reconstructing cross-skill dependencies, artifact flows, and capability compositions, and blocking the candidate skill when a chain-level risk is identified.

results.claim: Against six existing skill scanners, ColluSkill attains the highest average ASR (96.0%), showing that isolated per-skill scanning largely misses composition-based malicious behavior.
results.setting: Six skill scanners (CISCO, SkillFortify, Auditor, SlowMist, Vetter, SkillSpector); attacks generated with GPT-5.5; 200-payload multi-skill dataset
results.quote: Table 1 reports the ASR of different skill-based attacks against the evaluated skill scanners. Overall, ColluSkill achieves the highest ASR on almost all scanners, with an average ASR of 96.0%.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: Context-aware chain-level scanning (ChainGuard) reduces ColluSkill's average ASR from 96.0% to 22.5%, but not to zero.
results.setting: ChainGuard scanning each candidate skill with full installed-skill context; same 200-chain dataset; underlying model GPT-5.5
results.quote: The average ASR of ColluSkill against existing skill scanners is 96.0%, while the ASR drops to 22.5% under ChainGuard.
results.locator: Experiments / Main results (ChainGuard), Table 1 and Table 4

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: Adding installed-skill context to ChainGuard barely hurts benign workflows: the benign pass rate only decreases from 99.7% to 99.5%.
results.setting: ChainGuard with vs without full installed-skill context on benign workflows
results.quote: At the same time, installed-skill context has little effect on benign workflows. The pass rate decreases only from 99.7% to 99.5%.

results.claim: ColluSkill's gain does not come from naive payload splitting: chain planning raises the average ASR from 36.7% to 68.2%, and scanner-feedback refinement further raises it to 96.0%.
results.setting: Ablation over Naive Split / Chain Planning / Full ColluSkill on the same six scanners and 200-chain dataset
results.quote: Chain planning increases the average ASR from 36.7% to 68.2%, and scanner-feedback refinement further raises it to 96.0%.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: The first scanner-feedback refinement iteration delivers the largest stealth gain, raising the average ASR from 64.9% to 84.7%, with diminishing returns after about five iterations.
results.setting: Average ASR across the evaluated scanners at each refinement iteration (Figure 3)
results.quote: Before refinement, the ASR is only 64.9%. After the first refinement iteration, it quickly increases to 84.7%.
results.locator: Effect of LLM refinement iterations, Figure 3

denominator.how_counted: In the refinement experiment, we report the average ASR across the evaluated scanners at each iteration.

results.claim: ColluSkill attack chains execute at runtime across three coding agents and three model backbones, with chain activation success rates ranging from 58.5% to 92.5% (highest and most stable on OpenCode).
results.setting: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex agents with GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.2 model backbones
results.quote: As shown in Table 2, ColluSkill achieves the highest and most stable activation rates on OpenCode, ranging from 87.5% to 92.5%. The rates range from 62.0% to 78.2% on Claude Code and from 58.5% to 72.0% on Codex.

results.claim: Non-adversarial multi-skill composition alone is insufficient for scanner evasion: SCRBench reaches only 34.8% average ASR versus 96.0% for ColluSkill.
results.setting: SCRBench (multi-skill baseline) vs ColluSkill on the same six skill scanners
results.quote: SCRBench achieves an average ASR of 34.8%, compared with 96.0% for ColluSkill.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

limitations.statement: ChainGuard does not reduce ColluSkill's ASR to zero, so multi-skill attacks remain an open defense problem.
limitations.quote: Still, ChainGuard does not reduce the ASR to zero, which means that multi-skill attacks remain a challenging defense problem in practice.
